distributionSurfaces.description: Vite application JavaScript, CSS, fonts, workers, and repository-owned WebAssembly deployed to Cloudflare Pages, including the seven exact reviewed FLAC, Opus, Vorbis, WavPack, mpg123, LAME, and TwoLAME codec payloads imported by the browser codec composition.

Versioned optional non-codec assets fetched from assets.soundscaper.org rather than bundled into Pages. The checked-in FFmpeg WebAssembly publication manifests and audit scripts are retained legacy tooling only; the production browser does not import, package, publish, or fetch that runtime.
The desktop-specific Vite application copied into each Electron product; its composition excludes the Web FFmpeg wrapper and core runtime.

Translation and separately admitted runtime assets staged beside the Electron renderer, including exact reviewed libFLAC, libopus/libogg, libvorbis/libogg, WavPack, mpg123, LAME, and TwoLAME WebAssembly audio providers. Their runtime manifest authenticates each WASM file and its complete transitive JavaScript module closure before fresh supervised utility-process execution. Desktop targets whose assistance manifest row is built also stage the exact manifest-authenticated sherpa-onnx 1.13.5 local-assistance Node and native runtime. Application-supplied FFmpeg/libav, FFmpeg WebAssembly, and unqualified bundled WebM/AV1 payloads are excluded. Electron's separately inventoried alternate framework libffmpeg remains part of the Electron shell.

Electron, embedded Chromium and Node.js, Electron's exact alternate framework libffmpeg intended upstream to omit proprietary codec support, and the repository-owned main/preload process code. The framework library is not a Soundscaper codec-provider tier or patent-clearance evidence.

Public desktop packages, notices, checksums, and source archives required for content actually redistributed. Each package contains the seven exact reviewed compressed-audio WebAssembly providers, the exact verified Electron alternate framework libffmpeg for its target, and the target-supported manifest-authenticated sherpa-onnx 1.13.5 local-assistance Node and native runtime. Release assembly emits one preferred corresponding-source ZIP for those seven providers before SHA256SUMS: it fail-closed validates their exact shipped WASM identities, source manifests, upstream archives, Soundscaper wrappers, in-tree WavPack snapshot, build scripts and transitive helpers, configuration, relink instructions, and license texts, and records every included source byte in a deterministic internal receipt. This desktop source delivery does not enable any future reactivation of the retained legacy FFmpeg WebAssembly publication tooling. macOS ARM64 and Windows x64/ARM64 Soundscaper packages additionally require a target-native, canary-tested repository-owned operating-system codec addon whose exact manifest, payload, target, byte length, and SHA-256 are authenticated through staging and packaging; Linux has no OS codec payload and macOS x64 is unsupported. User-installed external FFmpeg remains outside this artifact closure and is not copied into the release set.

The development-only packages and publication records are retained to reproduce and audit historical evidence. They are outside the production browser dependency closure and no application artifact publishes, packages, imports, or fetches this runtime.

runtimeProvenance.upstreamIntent: Electron's matching alternate release asset is intended upstream to omit proprietary codec support.
runtimeProvenance.verification: Exact target, file type, byte length, and SHA-256 are verified. No complete codec inventory, behavior, absence-of-patent-exposure, or patent-clearance claim is made.

desktopCodecPolicy.patentPosition: No patent clearance or non-infringement representation is made for any codec, provider, use, or territory.

vendoredHeaders.rationale: The SPA format builders the native audio backend needs are static inline functions in the headers, so dlopen cannot reach them. Only headers are checked in; the library is resolved at runtime and never shipped.

distributionChecks.verification: A preferred deterministic corresponding-source ZIP is emitted and checksummed with every desktop release. It contains exact verified upstream source archives, the complete in-tree WavPack snapshot, Soundscaper wrappers, build scripts and transitive helpers, source configuration, relink/replacement instructions, and licenses for the seven exact shipped module identities. It does not authorize any future reactivation of the retained legacy FFmpeg WebAssembly publication tooling, Electron framework internals, OS providers, external FFmpeg, patent clearance, or non-infringement.

distributionChecks.blocker: No versioned web route or web artifact currently delivers the preferred corresponding source and relink or replacement instructions for the LGPL-covered mpg123, LAME, and TwoLAME payloads shipped in the Pages bundle.
No versioned web route or web artifact currently delivers THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.md with the deployed application and optional runtimes.

Any future reactivation of the retained legacy publication tooling remains blocked because its manifest identifies FFmpeg and ffmpeg.wasm archives but does not inventory and pin complete corresponding source for every enabled library in the binary.
Any future publication of the retained legacy core remains blocked because no distribution-specific, jurisdiction-specific patent review is recorded for its enabled codec set.

futureDistributionGates.blocker: The current Utility Gain conformance package is repository-owned application code in the closed release catalog; it does not admit an externally authored or non-repository-owned package or satisfy that package's inventory, source, notice, and review duties.

Seven exact reviewed compressed-audio WebAssembly providers are verified outside this future gate and execute in authenticated, isolated one-shot Electron utility processes: libFLAC, libopus/libogg, libvorbis/libogg, WavPack, mpg123, LAME, and TwoLAME. Specialized first-party PCM readers remain application code and libsndfile is not bundled. Windows Media Foundation and macOS ARM64 AudioToolbox use a target-native codec-only build for macOS ARM64, Windows x64, and Windows ARM64; the build runs native canaries, applies and checks the macOS ad-hoc execution seal before hashing, and staging, package, content-manifest, and startup checks bind one exact manifest and payload. Linux has no uniform OS tier and macOS x64 is unsupported. User-installed external FFmpeg has exact live-checked keyed-RGBA H.264/AAC MP4 and VP9/Opus WebM paths, but those external bytes remain outside the production artifact closure. There is no bundled or operating-system video provider and no libwebm, libvpx, dav1d, SVT-AV1, or libaom payload or AV1 execution path, so bundled and operating-system WebM/AV1 execution fails closed. Electron's exact alternate framework libffmpeg is Chromium infrastructure rather than a provider tier, while user-installed external FFmpeg remains outside the production artifact closure.

refusedLocalModels.reason: Verbatim transcription with filler-word timings is exactly the 7A-2 use case, but the weights forbid commercial use. Parakeet timing plus a filler lexicon replaces it.
The common forced aligner and every ONNX re-export inherit non-commercial terms from the upstream multilingual speech project. English realignment uses wav2vec2-base-960h instead.
End-to-end diarization with non-commercial weights; ONNX conversions inherit the restriction. The segmentation and embedding pipeline replaces it.
The original Canary release is non-commercial. The later flash and v2 refreshes are CC-BY-4.0 but add nothing over Parakeet for these products.
The madmom code is permissive but its trained models are non-commercial, which contaminates anything loading them. Beat This provides MIT beat and downbeat weights.

refusedLocalModels.license: Unstated, and depends on madmom inference
refusedLocalModels.reason: Weight terms are not stated and offline inference depends on the non-commercial madmom models.
Separation weights are non-commercial despite permissive code.
The additional conditions forbid deployment that competes with the vendor and restrict onward redistribution, so it is not redistributable here. Silero VAD replaces it.
The pretrained models are non-commercial. The AGPL code alone would be compatible with this product, but the weights are not redistributable.

No community checkpoint carries per-file terms and training-data provenance is undocumented, so no record can be completed. The anvuew dereverb_room checkpoint, whose repository does declare GPL-3.0 card metadata, is tracked separately as dereverb-room.
Checkpoints are published only through shared-drive links with no stable source, and the hosting repository has a history of per-model licence exceptions. PANNs CNN14 covers the same tagging need.

No weights licence grant exists from any source: the UVR repository has no LICENSE file despite README prose claiming MIT, no first-party model card exists on any mirror, and the model's author (FoxJoy) is uncredited in UVR's own credits. The dereverb-room record covers the need instead.
